# Pre-tax Deductions Process

Owner: Priya Nair

## Overview

Benefits sends each employee's elections to Payroll every pay period. Payroll deducts the per-period amount from gross pay.

## How amounts are calculated

The per-period deduction is the annual employee premium divided by the number of pay periods in the year. The deduction amount does not change with hours worked or overtime.

## Timing

Elections approved in BenHub before payroll cutoff are sent in that period's file. Later changes start the following period. Missed deductions are caught up over the next two periods, not in a single period.

## Eligibility changes

If an employee loses eligibility, BenHub sends a stop record, and deductions end with the last pay date in the coverage month.

# Benefits Eligibility Rules

Owner: Priya Nair · Maintained by: Marcus Hill · System: BenHub

## 1. Who is eligible

An employee is eligible for medical, dental, and vision coverage when they are a full-time employee, or a part-time employee who meets the hours threshold in section 2.

## 2. Hours threshold

### 2.1 Measurement

Eligibility hours are measured over each biweekly period. An employee meets the threshold when they have 60 or more eligible hours in the biweekly period, which equals an average of 30 hours per week. BenHub assumes all hours arrive as biweekly totals; it does not look at individual workweeks.

### 2.2 Which hours count

Benefits eligibility uses scheduled hours, not overtime hours. Overtime hours are excluded from the eligibility calculation so that a temporary overtime spike does not make an employee eligible and then ineligible again. Paid time off counts as eligible hours.

### 2.3 Look-back

Variable-hour employees are measured over a 12-month standard measurement period. If the average is 30 or more hours per week, coverage is offered for the following 12-month stability period.

## 3. Waiting period

Coverage begins on the first of the month after 60 days of employment.

## 4. Loss of eligibility

If an employee drops below the threshold for two consecutive biweekly periods and is not in a stability period, coverage ends at the end of the month. The employee is offered COBRA.

## 5. Inputs

BenHub receives hours from ClockLine every two weeks as a biweekly total per employee, split into scheduled hours and overtime hours.

# Design doc · New eligibility service

Author: Marcus Hill · Date: Oct 10, 2026 · Status: In review · Reviewers: Priya Nair

## Problem

Eligibility logic lives inside BenHub's enrollment code. It is hard to test, and other systems cannot ask "is this employee eligible?" without going through enrollment.

## Proposal

Build a new eligibility service: a standalone service that evaluates employee eligibility for benefits from hours, employment status, and waiting periods, and exposes the result through an API.

## Scope

- Rule definitions stored as versioned JSON
- Hours-based eligibility (biweekly measurement, look-back periods)
- Waiting periods and stability periods
- An API: `GET /eligibility/{employee}/{period}`

## Timeline

Build starts this sprint (Oct 13). Target: pilot clients in January 2027.

## Open questions

- Should other teams (Payroll) call this service instead of keeping their own eligibility checks? Not discussed with Payroll yet.
- How do retroactive hours changes affect a decision that was already made? Unknown, needs follow-up.

## Alternatives considered

- Keep logic in BenHub: rejected, not reusable.
- Buy a vendor rules engine: rejected on cost.

# Overtime Policy

Owner: Payroll · Effective: January 2026

## Purpose

This policy defines how Payroll calculates overtime pay for non-exempt employees.

## Workweek

The workweek is a fixed, recurring period of 168 hours, Sunday 12:00 a.m. through Saturday 11:59 p.m., unless a client configures a different start day.

## Calculation

Overtime is calculated weekly. Each workweek stands alone: hours are never averaged across two weeks, even when the pay period is biweekly. An employee who works 50 hours in week one and 30 hours in week two of a biweekly period is owed 10 hours of overtime, even though total hours equal 80.

Overtime is paid at 1.5 times the regular rate for hours worked over 40 in the workweek.

## Hours worked

Hours worked include all time the employee is required to be on duty. Paid time off, holidays, and sick time are not hours worked and do not count toward the 40-hour threshold.

## State rules

Some states require daily overtime (for example, over 8 hours in a day). PayCore applies state daily overtime rules when the client's work location requires it. Daily and weekly overtime are not paid twice for the same hour.

## Source of hours

Payroll uses the approved hours delivered by ClockLine. ClockLine identifies which hours are overtime; Payroll applies the rate. If ClockLine and PayCore disagree on overtime hours, PayCore uses ClockLine's hours and raises an exception.

## Questions

Contact Ana Torres for policy questions.

# Pay Schedule Guide

Owner: Ana Torres

## Supported frequencies

- Weekly: 52 pay dates per year
- Biweekly: 26 pay dates per year (most common)
- Semimonthly: 24 pay dates per year, on the 15th and last day of the month

## Cutoffs

Payroll cutoff is 5:00 p.m. Eastern, two business days before the pay date. ClockLine sends the final approved hours file at cutoff. Changes after cutoff go into the next pay period.

## Holidays

If a pay date falls on a bank holiday, the pay date moves to the previous business day and cutoff moves one business day earlier.

## Off-cycle runs

Off-cycle runs are allowed for terminations and corrections. They require approval from a payroll lead.

# Payroll Calculation Guide

Owner: Ana Torres · Last reviewed: September 2026 · System: PayCore

This guide describes how PayCore turns approved hours and earnings into net pay. It covers the standard gross-to-net sequence only. Corrections to prior pay periods are handled separately and are not covered here.

## 1. Inputs

PayCore receives three inputs each pay period:

1. Approved hours from ClockLine (Time & Attendance), delivered as a nightly file and a final file at payroll cutoff.
2. Earnings and deduction elections from BenHub (Benefits).
3. Employee pay setup: pay rate, pay frequency, and tax profile.

## 2. Pay frequency

Most clients run biweekly payroll. Weekly and semimonthly schedules are supported. See the Pay Schedule Guide for cutoffs.

## 3. Regular earnings

Regular earnings equal regular hours multiplied by the base hourly rate. Salaried employees receive their period salary regardless of hours, unless they are non-exempt.

## 4. Gross pay

### 4.1 Earning types

Gross pay is the sum of regular earnings, overtime earnings, shift differentials, bonuses, and commissions for the period.

### 4.2 Overtime in gross pay

Overtime earnings are added to gross pay before any deductions are taken. Pre-tax benefit deductions are calculated on total gross pay, including overtime. Overtime premiums are calculated at 1.5 times the regular rate of pay for hours over 40 in a workweek, as defined in the Overtime Policy.

### 4.3 Regular rate

The regular rate includes non-discretionary bonuses and shift differentials. When a bonus covers several workweeks, PayCore allocates it across those weeks before computing the overtime premium.

## 5. Deductions

### 5.1 Order of deductions

1. Pre-tax deductions (medical, dental, vision premiums, HSA, FSA, pre-tax 401(k)).
2. Taxes, calculated on taxable wages after pre-tax deductions.
3. Post-tax deductions (Roth 401(k), voluntary life, garnishments).

### 5.2 Deduction amounts

Deduction amounts come from BenHub. PayCore does not decide whether an employee is eligible for a benefit; it applies the elections BenHub sends.

## 6. Taxes

See the Tax Withholding Guide for federal, state, and local withholding rules.

## 7. Net pay

Net pay equals gross pay minus all deductions and taxes. If net pay would be negative, PayCore stops the check and creates a payroll exception for review.

## 8. Exceptions

Payroll exceptions appear on the exceptions dashboard. Common exceptions: missing tax profile, negative net pay, hours over 80 in a single week, and missing pay rate. Exceptions must be cleared before payroll cutoff.

# Payroll FAQ

Note: some answers below have not been reviewed since 2024.

**When is unused PTO paid out after an employee leaves?**
Unused PTO is paid on the employee's final paycheck, issued in an off-cycle run on the last day of work.

**Can an employee change their direct deposit mid-period?**
Yes. Changes made before cutoff apply to the current period.

**Why does an employee's overtime look different on their pay statement than in ClockLine?**
PayCore shows overtime pay, not overtime hours. Divide by 1.5 times the regular rate to compare.

**Do we still support paper checks?**
Yes, but they are being phased out in 2024. (Outdated: paper checks are still supported as of 2026.)

**How do I correct last period's overtime?**
Contact the payroll help channel.

**What is the cutoff time?**
Cutoff is 3:00 p.m. Eastern. (Outdated: cutoff moved to 5:00 p.m. Eastern. See the Pay Schedule Guide.)

# Retro pay questions (copied from the #payroll-help channel)

These are informal notes copied from team chat. They are not reviewed documentation.

---

**Mar 4** · Question from the support desk: a client's rate increase was entered late and is now effective three pay periods back. Do we redo overtime too?

**Maria Lopez:** Yes. When a rate change is backdated, the overtime premium for every affected week has to be recalculated at the new regular rate. People forget this. I run the retro calc week by week, not for the whole period at once.

---

**May 19** · Question from Raj: why don't we just compute the retro amount as rate difference times total hours?

**Maria Lopez:** Because overtime hours need the 1.5x premium applied to the difference. Rate difference times total hours underpays anyone with overtime in those weeks. I handle those manually in the retro worksheet.

---

**Jul 22** · Question from a new analyst: where is the retro pay process written down?

**Maria Lopez:** It isn't, honestly. Ask me and I'll walk you through it. I keep meaning to write it up.

---

**Aug 30** · Question from the support desk: retro correction for a timesheet that was fixed after payroll closed. Overtime changed from 2 to 6 hours.

**Maria Lopez:** Pay the 4 extra overtime hours in the next regular run as a retro earning, coded RETRO-OT so it shows separately on the pay statement. Don't reopen the closed period.

# Tax Withholding Guide

Owner: Payroll · Entry type: regulation

## Federal income tax

PayCore calculates federal income tax using the employee's current W-4 elections and the IRS percentage method tables for the pay frequency.

## Social Security and Medicare

Social Security is withheld at 6.2% up to the annual wage base. Medicare is withheld at 1.45% on all wages, plus an additional 0.9% on wages over $200,000 in the calendar year.

## Pre-tax deductions

Section 125 deductions (medical, dental, vision, FSA, HSA through payroll) reduce wages for federal income tax, Social Security, and Medicare. Pre-tax 401(k) reduces wages for federal income tax only.

## Supplemental wages

Bonuses and retro earnings paid separately may use the 22% flat supplemental rate.

## State and local

State withholding uses the work location's state rules. Reciprocity agreements are applied when the employee lives and works in different states.

# Design doc · ClockLine overtime calculator

Author: Sam Okafor · Status: Shipped (June 2026)

## Summary

ClockLine has a built-in overtime calculator. It computes weekly overtime, state daily overtime, and double time from raw punches, and it is in production for all clients as of June 2026.

## What it does

- Splits each workweek's hours into regular, overtime, and double time
- Applies state daily overtime rules (for example, over 8 hours in a day)
- Never pays daily and weekly overtime for the same hour
- Handles configurable workweek start days

The calculator is exposed as an internal API: `POST /overtime/calculate` with raw punches for a workweek, returning the regular/overtime/double-time split. Any team can call it. Today only ClockLine's own export uses it.

1,800 rule test cases covering all 50 states.

# Punch Rounding Rules

Owner: Sam Okafor

## Current rule

ClockLine rounds each punch to the nearest 6 minutes (one tenth of an hour). A punch at 8:02 rounds to 8:00; a punch at 8:04 rounds to 8:06.

## Neutrality

Rounding must be neutral over time: it cannot consistently favor the employer.

## Effect on overtime

Rounded punches are the hours used for the overtime calculator and for the hours files sent to Payroll and Benefits. Any change to the rounding interval changes overtime hours downstream.

## Proposed change (under discussion)

Product has proposed rounding to the nearest 15 minutes instead of 6, to match a large client's policy. No decision yet.
